item.title: 5 of the unluckiest plays in sports history to revisit in honor of Friday the 13th
item.description: From Leon Lett's Super Bowl fumble to the Kick Six, these five unlucky plays prove Friday the 13th has nothing on sports history's cruelest moments.
item.content:encoded:
Friday the 13th. A day synonymous with bad luck and people who genuinely believe walking under a ladder might ruin their entire existence.

Over the centuries, sports have proven a twisted sense of humor. Bad luck runs rampant. You can practice your entire life to hone your skills, execute a play almost perfectly, and still end up on the wrong side of a moment so ridiculously unfortunate that it feels like someone upstairs is playing a practical joke.

And in honor of Friday the 13th, we're counting down five of the most unlucky, bizarre and downright cruel plays in sports history.

DUKE'S BEATDOWN OF NC STATE INCLUDED A MUST-SEE MISSED FIELD GOAL RETURNED FOR A 109-YARD TOUCHDOWN

Imagine being the No. 1 team in college football, having national championship aspirations and watching your season take a devastating turn because of a missed field goal.

Welcome to Alabama's nightmare.

With the 2013 Iron Bowl tied at 28 and just one second remaining, Nick Saban sent freshman kicker Adam Griffith onto the field to attempt a 57-yard field goal against Auburn.

What could possibly go wrong?

Griffith's kick fell short, landing in the hands of Auburn's Chris Davis, who was standing in the end zone specifically for this possibility.

Davis proceeded to sprint 109 yards for a touchdown as the Auburn crowd erupted into absolute pandemonium and stormed the field.

The Crimson Tide didn't just lose a football game. They watched their hopes of a third consecutive national championship disappear as Davis sprinted down the sideline.

For 86 years, the Boston Red Sox couldn't win a World Series.

And for a long time, their fans blamed a certain trade involving a certain baseball player with certain significance, named Babe Ruth.

The infamous "Curse of the Bambino" had become part of Boston sports folklore, and the 1986 World Series provided perhaps its cruelest chapter of that saga.

Leading the New York Mets 3-2 in the series, Boston was one out away from winning its first championship since 1918 during Game 6.

Then everything fell apart.

The Mets tied the game in the 10th inning, and with the winning run on second base, Mookie Wilson hit a slow ground ball toward Red Sox first baseman Bill Buckner.

It should have been a routine play. Instead, the baseball rolled directly between Buckner's legs, allowing Ray Knight to score the winning run.

Game over.

The fat lady had sung. The Mets won Game 7, and Buckner's error became one of the most infamous moments in baseball history.

To be fair, Boston had already blown its lead before Buckner's mistake, and the Red Sox still had another game to win the championship, but whether you want to call it poor concentration or bad luck, it's one of the most brutal plays you'll ever watch, unless you're a Yankees or Mets fan.

YANKEES INFIELDERS COLLIDE, ALLOWING METS TO SCORE GAME-WINNING RUN IN DRAMATIC COMEBACK

There are missed field goals.

There are heartbreaking missed field goals.

And then there's whatever supernatural, if you will, nonsense happened to Chicago Bears kicker Cody Parkey during the 2018 NFL playoffs.

On Jan. 6, 2019, the Bears trailed the Philadelphia Eagles 16-15 in the final seconds of their NFC Wild Card matchup.

Parkey lined up for a 43-yard field goal that would send Chicago into the divisional round.

The kick went up.

DOINK.

The football struck the left upright.

DOINK.

Then it bounced off the crossbar, falling into the end zone.

The Bears' season was over.

To make matters even more painful, Eagles defensive lineman Treyvon Hester had gotten a fingertip on the football, meaning the kick was officially ruled blocked.

Parkey had already hit the uprights four times in a single game earlier that season, making this an almost comically cruel conclusion.

One doink is unfortunate. Two doinks on the same kick, with your season hanging in the balance is about as unlucky as you can get.

VANDERBILT PULLED OFF THE MOST IMPROBABLE LAST-SECOND VICTORY YOU'LL EVER SEE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL

If Friday the 13th had an official baseball highlight, this would be it.

On May 26, 1993, Texas Rangers' outfielder José Canseco was tracking a deep fly ball hit by Cleveland's Carlos Martínez.

Canseco drifted back toward the warning track, positioned himself near the wall and prepared to make what appeared to be a fairly ordinary defensive play.

Instead, the baseball struck him directly on the noggin and sailed over the outfield fence for a home run.

Canseco didn't just fail to make the catch. He somehow transformed a fly ball into one of the most embarrassing home runs in MLB history.

It was comical and unlucky at the same time.

Canseco got one baseball to the dome and a lifetime of internet humiliation.

There are few things more embarrassing than celebrating a touchdown before actually scoring it. We've seen far too many bonehead plays where players drop the ball before the goal line.

Just ask former Dallas Cowboys defensive lineman Leon Lett.

During Super Bowl XXVII against the Buffalo Bills, Lett recovered a fumble and began rumbling toward the end zone for what appeared to be an easy defensive touchdown.

The Cowboys were already dominating the Bills, and Lett was about to add another six points to the scoreboard. It would have been his lone touchdown in his career.

There was just one tiny problem. He forgot that the play wasn't over.

As Lett approached the goal line, he slowed down and began holding the football away from his body in celebration.

Meanwhile, Buffalo receiver Don Beebe sprinted after him like his life depended on it, caught Lett just before the goal line and knocked the football out of his hand. The ball rolled through the end zone for a touchback.

Lett went from Super Bowl glory to an all-time blooper.

The good news? Dallas still won the game 52-17.

The bad news? More than three decades later, people still remember the defensive lineman who managed to fumble away a touchdown while celebrating it.

And as if the football gods weren't finished tormenting him, Lett became the central figure in another bizarre play later that year when he touched a blocked field goal in the snow against the Miami Dolphins, allowing Miami to recover and eventually kick the game-winner.

Two legendary football blunders in one calendar year? Yikes.

Sports are supposed to reward preparation, execution and talent. But every once in a while, the sports gods decide to throw a wrench into that equation.

Happy Friday the 13th, sports fans. Watch out for black cats, avoid walking under ladders and, whatever you do, hold onto the football until you're actually in the end zone.

item.title: Severe allergic reaction after sipping energy drink traced to unexpected source
item.description: A teen's severe allergic reaction to an energy drink was traced to cod collagen, revealing how fish-derived ingredients can hide in unexpected products.
item.content:encoded:
Anaphylaxis – a severe, potentially life-threatening allergic reaction – is usually tied to peanuts or shellfish, but a recent case has brought up a new concern.

According to a report by the American College of Allergy, Asthma and Immunology (ACAAI), a teen experienced a severe allergic reaction from an energy drink.

The case, which was presented at the ACAAI’s 2026 Annual Scientific Meeting held Nov. 12–16 in Phoenix, Arizona, involved a 15-year-old boy who developed "widespread hives," wheezing and difficulty breathing after trying a new beverage.

POPULAR DRINKS LINKED TO HEART ATTACKS, CARDIAC ARREST IN YOUNG ADULTS, STUDY FINDS

The teen was reportedly taken to the hospital, where he received two doses of epinephrine, albuterol — a medication commonly used in rescue inhalers to help open the airways — an antihistamine and IV fluids. His symptoms resolved after treatment.

A review of the drink’s label revealed that it contained 5 grams of collagen derived from cod.

According to the report, the teen reported mild throat itching and lip swelling when eating canned tuna, although he had eaten salmon without an issue. He also has eczema, asthma and allergic rhinitis (commonly called hay fever).

WHY STACKING SUPPLEMENTS WITHOUT A BLOOD TEST FIRST CAN DO MORE HARM THAN GOOD

Despite the teen's symptoms, a skin prick testing for tuna, cod and flounder allergy all returned negative.

These findings represent initial research presented at the ACAAI conference, and have not yet been published in a peer-reviewed journal.

Allergist Annabelle Rowland, M.D., study author and ACAAI member based in Georgia, commented in a news release that this case shows "how tricky fish allergy can be."

"Collagen from fish is showing up in a growing number of products, from drinks to supplements," she said. "Standard fish allergy tests mostly look for a different fish protein and contain very little collagen, so a person can test negative and still react."

In a statement sent to Fox News Digital, a spokesperson for the Council for Responsible Nutrition in Washington, D.C., said that collagen ingredients can come from several animal sources, like fish, cattle and pigs.

"While collagen has been studied for potential benefits related to skin and joint health, consumers should consider their individual health needs and sensitivities when choosing products," they advised.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"Fish-derived collagen can pose an allergy risk for people sensitive to fish, and processing or hydrolysis does not necessarily eliminate that risk."

The spokesperson recommended those with fish allergies should carefully review product labels, which are required to identify major food allergens, such as fish. Consumers should also consult with their healthcare provider before considering these products.

"The case presented at ACAAI highlights the importance of allergen awareness, but a single suspected reaction does not establish how frequently such reactions occur," they added.

"Product manufacturers are required by law to provide accurate ingredient information and major allergen disclosures so consumers can make informed choices."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Sung Poblete, Ph.D., CEO of Virginia-based Food Allergy Research & Education, told Fox News Digital that fish collagen is increasingly being used in products like supplements, beverages and wellness items.

"While many people with fish allergy avoid all finned fish, reactions can vary between individuals and between different fish-derived proteins," she said. "So someone can be allergic to one type of fin fish and not another."

Poblete added that labels must identify the species of fish. Crustacean shellfish, such as shrimp, crab and lobster, must also be specifically identified, according to the FDA.

"For someone managing fish or shellfish allergy, 'marine collagen' on a label calls for a closer look at the ingredient list and 'contains' statement," she said. "If the source still isn’t clear, FARE encourages people to call the manufacturer before using the product."

Consumers are encouraged to ask the manufacturer what the collagen is made from, and how the product is sourced, packaged and tested for allergens.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"This case offers a timely reminder to read every label, including on drinks and supplements, and talk with an allergist about any reaction, even if a test came back negative," Poblete added.

Fox News Digital reached out to energy drink manufacturers for comment.

item.title: Is it weird for a coach to not talk to his team after a game, or is it extremely weird?
item.description: Auston Matthews revealed that Maple Leafs coach Jim Hiller doesn't usually talk to the team after games, raising eyebrows as Toronto sits 8-11-2.
item.content:encoded:
There are some things in sports that I thought were completely universal to the point that I never even think about them. One of them is a coach talking to their team after a game.

I had assumed this happened about 99.99% of the time. Sure, you might occasionally get the cold shoulder after an abysmal effort to send a message, but that's still communication.

However, an NHL bench boss is getting some attention after one of his players revealed that he normally doesn't talk to the team after games.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Toronto Maple Leafs captain Auston Matthews addressed the media after his team's 5-2 loss to the Minnesota Wild on Thursday, and that's when he said that head coach Jim Hiller doesn't usually talk to the team after games.

"He usually doesn’t speak after games, so I’m sure we’ll continue to try to clean some stuff up, go over video and make adjustments," Matthews said. "At the end of the day, it’s just minimizing those big mistakes or turnovers, especially against other teams’ top lines."

Uhh... I didn't realize that was optional.

Not even a "Good effort tonight, boys," when things are cooking, or a "You dopes are going to be bag skating tomorrow," after a brutal loss?

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I literally can't picture this happening in the NFL. Imagine if after a game they did the requisite cut to the locker room and everyone was just sitting around taking off their pads and shooting their game jerseys into the laundry bin because the coach was like, "Meh, I'm not talking."

I would find it awkward not to say something.

Coaching is all about communication, and not talking to the fellas after a game seems like an odd approach.

But hey, if it's working then... oh, it's not working.

This tidbit of info is not one that earned Hiller many fans, as the Leafs — always under the microscope as they are — are 8-11-2 on the year and sitting in seventh place in the Atlantic Division.

item.description: T-Mobile's T-Mix plans let new and existing customers get the Samsung Galaxy S26+ or Samsung Galaxy S26 for $0 upfront with no trade-in required.
item.content:encoded:
New and existing T-Mobile customers can score the Samsung Galaxy S26+ and the Samsung Galaxy S26 for $0 upfront with a qualifying T-Mix plan. Options include Standard, More and Loaded plans, which offer benefits like access to entertainment and streaming apps, delivery services and more.

Take advantage of one of the hottest cell phone deals on the market right now: a Samsung Galaxy S26+ for $0 upfront. For a limited time, shoppers can get the phone when they enroll in a qualifying T-Mix plan — with no trade-in required. Enjoy fast charging, a versatile triple rear camera system and AI tools like Photo Assist, Creative Studio and more.

If you prefer a compact, lightweight phone that’s easy to handle with one hand and fits into smaller pockets, the Galaxy S26 is worth a look. Shoppers can get it now for $0 upfront when they choose a qualifying T-Mix plan.

SCORE THE IPHONE 18 PRO ON T-MOBILE, NO TRADE-IN REQUIRED — PLUS OTHER PERKS

T-Mobile’s new customizable plans include Standard, More and Loaded, each with different tiers, features and number of Picks. Customers can use Picks as tokens that unlock benefits such as Netflix, Hulu, Apple Music, DoorDash, Google Gemini, Xbox Game Pass and device promotions.

The entry-level option, T-Mix Standard, costs $55 per month for one line and includes unlimited talk, text and data, plus 50GB of premium data and one Pick to use on an eligible benefit or device promotion.

The mid-tier option, T-Mix More, costs $75 per month for one line and comes with two Picks, unlimited premium data and 60GB of high-speed hotspot data.

The top-tier option, T-Mix Loaded, costs $95 per month for one line and includes three Picks, unlimited premium data, 250GB of high-speed hotspot data, up to 4K UHD streaming and $5 watch and tablet lines.
